# Kyoto Notes

## Overview

Four nights in Kyoto in late March 2024, based in a small machiya rental near Gojo. I went for the gardens rather than the temples, though the two overlap so much that the distinction hardly matters. Crowds were heavy at the famous spots before nine in the morning and again after four, so I planned each day around those windows. The weather turned warm and wet, and cherry season arrived about a week early.

## Gardens

The Philosopher's Path follows a canal in the north of the city and takes about half an hour at an easy walk. I started at the Ginkaku-ji end just after opening and had long stretches almost to myself. Moss gardens were the surprise of the trip. I gave a whole afternoon to the eastern hills, and the Kodaiji garden pass costs 2000 yen, which covers the main hall, the bamboo grove and the small museum. It was worth it for the rock garden alone. Ryoan-ji was busier than I expected, and I preferred the quieter plots at Daitoku-ji, where one ticket often opened three or four separate temple gardens.

## Notes

Cash still matters at the smaller gardens and shops. Carry coins for the bus, or buy a day pass at the station. Visits to the popular moss temple need a postcard or an online slot booked weeks ahead. I walked 14 km on the busiest day and my feet let me know about it. Early mornings beat every clever trick for avoiding queues, and the buses fill long before the temples open. A small tabi sock in my day bag saved me more than once at the stepping-stone entries. I kept a paper map alongside the phone app, because the app drained battery fast on a full day of walking.
